version.changelog:
AgentCanary 1.0.1 — Major Expansion & Endpoint Redesign

Multi-chain deposit support

• USDC/USDT accepted on Base, Ethereum, Arbitrum, Optimism, and Polygon
• Same deposit address on all chains — server auto-detects which chain the payment came from

Security hardening

• Helmet.js security headers (XSS protection, HSTS, X-Powered-By removed)
• 1MB request body limit
• Key creation rate limited: 5 attempts per 15 min per IP
• Global error isolation (uncaughtException/unhandledRejection handlers, no stack traces in responses)
• Fresh VirusTotal scan: 0/62 detections

New endpoints

• /api/central-banks — balance sheets, BTC reserves, stablecoin holdings, gold reserves, TIC data
• /api/predictions — Polymarket scenario probabilities + movers
• /api/expectations — rotation, crowding, early signals
• /api/institutional/13f — 13F filings, short interest, CFTC COT
• /api/defi/signals — DeFi-specific signal aggregation
• /api/btc-options/skew — options skew data
• /api/premiums/coinbase, /api/premiums/kimchi — individual premium endpoints
• /api/sentiment/reddit — 14 subreddit sentiment analysis
• /api/mean-reversion/* — signals, trades, stats
• /api/hindenburg — Hindenburg omen + history
• /api/cape — CAPE ratio
• /api/crypto-reentry — crypto re-entry framework + history
• /api/kill-conditions — kill switch conditions

Infrastructure

• OpenAPI spec expanded: 92 → 121 paths
• Interactive Swagger UI at api.agentcanary.ai/api/docs
• Minimum deposit lowered: $10 → $5

vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: agentcanary
Version: 1.0.1

The skill bundle consists entirely of documentation and metadata for an external financial intelligence API (api.agentcanary.ai). It contains no executable code, local filesystem access, or malicious instructions. The instructions provided in SKILL.md and references/endpoints.md are focused on guiding the AI agent to fetch market data, macro regime classifications, and trading signals, which is consistent with the tool's stated purpose. Authentication is handled via wallet-based API keys, and the documentation emphasizes security measures such as read-only access and the absence of local execution.

llm.summary: The skill is an instruction-only API integration for a market-intelligence service and its declared requirements and instructions are internally consistent with that purpose, with only minor bookkeeping/clarity issues.

dimensions.detail: The name/description match the provided SKILL.md and endpoint reference: a JSON HTTP API for market intelligence. The skill requests no system binaries, no environment variables, and no installs — which is appropriate for an API-only integration that operates over HTTPS with wallet-based API keys.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Instructions are limited to making HTTP GET/POST requests to the listed endpoints and a recommended polling pattern for risk signals. This stays within the stated purpose. Minor note: the SKILL.md repeatedly states 'No secrets in prompt' but does not provide guidance for how agents should securely store/use the API key (it uses ?apikey=... as query param). The file also includes behavioral guidance (e.g., 'If Risk-Off → suppress trading'), which is within scope but means the skill can influence agent decision flows — not an incoherence, just a capability to be aware of.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Instruction-only skill with no install spec and no code files; nothing is written to disk and nothing is downloaded, which is the lowest-risk installation model.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The API requires an API key generated via wallet deposit, but the registry metadata lists no required env vars or primary credential. This is a minor mismatch (the skill expects a runtime API key but doesn't declare a primaryEnv), not evidence of malicious behavior. No unrelated secrets or credentials are requested.

dimensions.detail: always is false and the skill has no install footprint and does not request persistent system privileges. Autonomous model invocation is allowed (platform default) but not combined with any elevated local privileges.

llm.guidance: This skill appears to be a straightforward, instruction-only API integration for market intelligence. Before installing/use, consider: 1) The service uses wallet-based payments — you must deposit USDC/USDT to create a key; verify the service (TLS, domain, reputation) before sending funds and start with a small deposit to test. 2) The API key is used as a query parameter (?apikey=...), so do NOT paste it into model prompts or logs; store it securely (agent runtime secret store or environment variable) and ensure the agent makes HTTP calls outside the LLM context. 3) The SKILL.md does not declare a primaryEnv for the API key — confirm how your agent runtime will supply the key safely. 4) The skill can influence agent trading behavior via its 'Default Agent Pattern' — treat signals as advisory and ensure your agent has explicit guardrails for risk control and execution. 5) No local code/install reduces filesystem risk, but you should still verify the external endpoints (https://api.agentcanary.ai and app pages) and review billing/withdrawal policies, since payments are custodial. If you want higher assurance, ask for independent verification of the service (company/legal pages, independent reviews) or test with minimal funds.
